content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (MINCOMMIT)** — submitted.

**What the document does:** Section 8.1(ii) sets a "minimum monthly fee (Monthly Base Fee)," and Section 10.3(A) requires Tri City to obtain *all* bundled Services from M&I "during the Term" — which runs eight years (p0049). There is no volume-reduction or partial-termination right on our side, while M&I may withdraw non-Core Services on 90 days' notice (10.2). The minimum also drives Estimated Remaining Value (p0039), which sets the Section 11.1/11.2 termination fees, so the only exit is one year's notice plus a percentage of the remaining minimums — a penalty rather than a true-up.

**Why it fails the fallback:** the fallback tolerates a commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up. This is a multi-year take-or-pay with neither reduction nor a penalty-free exit.

**Redline (validated, fallback level):** amended 10.3(A) so the sourcing commitment runs only through the then-current twelve-month period, is reducible on 30 days' notice, and triggers an equitable reduction of the Monthly Base Fee with no shortfall or penalty charge. We did not push the preferred position (no minimum at all) because that would unwind the bundled pricing bargain.
